utterances.text: Thank you, General. If we could refer to page 2, the part which shows the signature. Could you confirm for us there that it states that it is -- the name at the bottom is "Sefer Halilovic." However, if we look to the left, and we can see four initials there, we see the abbreviation "DJ." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that you signed this order on behalf of General Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, and the "DJ" here indicates that I wrote it. So the initials -- the first initials are of the person who writes the document, and the second initials are of the typist. Every document, every military document, has to indicate its author and its typist. And as for this part which says "For the Chief," I signed it on his authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we could please return back to page one, and it's point 2 that I'm interested in with a list of names.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, would you agree with me that the men named in this order were the most educated military officers from the Main Staff of the Bosnian Army, or certain among them?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would. They are the ranks of the most educated officers, of military specialists, for the duties assigned to them, which they were to discharge in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's correct, is it not, General, that General Siber was in command of IKM Zenica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't see that from this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You can't see it from this document, General, but did you know was General Siber at Zenica IKM?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the forward command post. Siber was issued the task -- I don't know the details -- to coordinate activities in the Zenica area during the conflict between the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the forces of the HVO, but I don't know much about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt the flow here, but can the record be corrected? "IKM," it's an "I." I think everybody agrees with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I did notice that. Maybe if you could refer to it as "IKM" rather than "EKM."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. During your evidence, General, you've mentioned that a command post was established at Kakanj. I'd like to ask you some questions about that, if I may. Could we please show the witness Exhibit 279. And while we're waiting for it to come up on the screen, if I can just explain that this is an order from Rasim Delic to all administrations, dated the 26th of November, 1993. General, please, could you look at the first three paragraphs? The first one begins: "In accordance with the needs of the situation in the BH theatre of war ..."

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. This is for a planned relocation of a part of the Staff of the Supreme Command to free territory, and the chief of the Main Staff of the Armed Forces and chiefs of administration are to immediately begin organisational, professional, material preparations to carry out this task, and the team is set up in order to prepare the facilities and the area for a forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: As one of the deputy commanders, were you familiar with this order?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in its written form, as a document, but I was aware of the commander's decision for a command post of the Supreme Command Staff to be set up outside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, although this document does not refer to Kakanj, was it well known amongst the Main Staff that the command post which would be established would be located at Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the exact moment when this was ordered, I don't think so, because they were given the task to choose the post -- the position of a new forward command post of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In any event, we know that a location was selected at Kakanj; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is so, excellent conditions were created there for accommodating the command post of the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just for clarification, at the time that the command post was set up, Enver Hadzihasanovic was the chief of the Main Staff; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not the commander of the Main Staff, the chief of the Main Staff. As far as I know, Sefer Halilovic was still the chief of the Main Staff at that time, to the best of my knowledge. So as far as I can remember. It doesn't mean that I am necessarily right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can put this document away. Could we please refer to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Do you have the end of this document so that I could see?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Please, if the General could be shown the second page. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's perfectly all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So we can see from this document, General, that it was signed by Rasim Delic; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is signed by him, but allow me -- you cannot gather from this document who the chief of the Main Staff is, and I still believe that at the time it was still Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can move to the next document, Exhibit 281. This is an order from General Delic dated the 16th of February, 1994, to the chiefs of Administration of the ARBiH. And I apologise for the quality of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you see this? Can you make out the document, General?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just very unclear. If you can make my work easier, perhaps you could read out portions for me, because I can hardly make out anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'll do that, General. Before I come to the content of the document, perhaps, please, if we could look at the second page to see -- to confirm who it is from.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was also signed by the army commander, Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, if I can refer you back to the first page and the first paragraph. It's the section that begins: "Because of the needs personally observed in the liberated territories, the requirement for further command of armed combat ...", et cetera, et cetera, "it is necessary for the VK OS Staff to remain in the field." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under "(a)" it says: "Deputies and assistant commanders in accordance with the commander's decision." And then "(b)": "They are to be deployed in the general area of Kakanj, Binjezevo, Zenica, the Staff of Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the operations department of ... preparations for different operations --"

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Before we go into the details, I'd just like to clarify something in that first paragraph that you read. Where it says "VK OS Staff," is that the same as the Main Staff or the SVK?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not the same. The Main Staff refers just to the structures of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Supreme Command Staff refers to the civilian and military leadership, and that staff, in addition to members of the army, commanders sent deputies, perhaps two or three assistants, also comprised representatives of the Ministry of the Interior and some other factors, I believe also the civilian protection minister. The Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina consisted of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Ministry of the Interior, of Civilian Protection, and of other defence entities or factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we look at the paragraph underneath the one that I've just read to you or referred to, there it states: "We should repeat once again the well-known fact that the Supreme Command, the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, is located in Sarajevo, and its members, if judged necessary, in the field." And then the order goes on at part B to specify where the organs of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina Staff and the Administrations are to be deployed; is that right? We can see that it states that they are to be deployed in the wider sector of Kakanj, Binjezevo village and Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So would you agree that this order is, in effect, an order continuing KM Kakanj? In other words, it's an order that KM Kakanj is to continue fulfilling its function?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the command post was definitely set up of the Staff of the Supreme Command in Kakanj, with the possibility of its efficient functioning and not as previously, as up to that point, as theretofore.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, and you mentioned this a little earlier, that amongst the organs deployed within KM Kakanj is the Operations Centre which was responsible for the planning, preparation, organisation, monitoring and commanding of combat operations; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General, I wonder if you can help us clarify the difference between an IKM and KM Kakanj. Would you agree with me that an IKM is just a temporary location which the ARBiH used for a short period of time or as long as necessary for it to fulfill a specific function?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Similarly, an IKM would only be staffed with the minimum number of officers necessary for it to carry out its task or objective?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In contrast to an IKM, is it right that KM Kakanj was established on a long-term basis, so from December 1993 up until the end of the war in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And also in the case of KM Kakanj, the majority of the officers from the Main Staff were relocated there as well?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your evidence that, and this must be following the establishment of KM Kakanj, a smaller group was in Sarajevo and there was a larger group in Kakanj. Is that --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If I can focus on the smaller group in Sarajevo, would you agree with me that once the majority of the Main Staff relocated to Kakanj, the role of the Operations Centre in Sarajevo was greatly reduced?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown document D240. While we're waiting for it to appear on the screen, this document is a report dated the 15th of February, 1994, from the Operations Centre at Sarajevo to the Chief of the Main Staff, Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps, first of all, we could start by -- well, first of all, General, do you see this document and the date that it bears?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 15th of February, 1994, Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Supreme Command Staff of the Armed Forces, Operations Command Centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we could please look to page 2 just to confirm who the document is from. It's the same page, the same in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is signed by Zicro Suljevic, who was in the Operations Centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can turn back to the first page. It's the second paragraph that I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General, what this letter says, from Mr. Suljevic, is: "I held a meeting with the remaining OCK in Sarajevo. Fehim --"

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commanding, of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: "Fehim, illegible, and Zineta Mehovic are doing the regular work. They are working on filing the written documents from 1993. Paravalic is writing his memoirs and newspaper articles for "Oslobodjenje." Milo Loncarevic is in his apartment. He is not engaged anywhere and is working on relocating to the territory of Croatia. Sila Dzambasovic sometimes comes over to the SDK when Paravalic needs the text of his memoirs or for the newspapers retyped." First of all, General, do you know who all of those men are who are mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And is it correct to say that they all worked in the Operations Centre at the Command in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this document shows that those men working in the Operations Centre, in the centre, had very little to do? One was writing his memoirs and the other stayed at home in his apartment.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems to be so, according to this report here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And two of the other men were carrying out filing duties, filing documents from 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was their duty, to file documents. These were the people from the typist pool who were actually working on documents, their typing and filing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this document reflects the fact that in the Operations Centre at Sarajevo, the officers based there did not have a great deal of work to carry out?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was as much work as was requested from us to do from the command post in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then, finally, before we leave this document, if we can look at the third paragraph down, it says: "Otherwise, the work of other organs in this building is also disorganized; they come to work and leave as they please." Does that sentence reflect the situation occurring in other organs within the Command in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not -- not necessarily, but a report of -- this kind of a report from Zicro Suljevic comes as a surprise to me, because he had been appointed building commander already in February or March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. I'd now like to turn to a different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I tender it for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Turning to a different issue, General, I'd now like to ask you about the appointment of General Delic on the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And in this context if we could please show the witness Exhibit 315. While we're waiting for the document to appear, I can explain that this document is the minutes of the 203rd Presidency session that took place on the 8th of June, 1993. Please, could we turn to page 2 of both the English and B/C/S documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: First of all, General, can you help us? Does this look to you as if these are minutes of a Presidency session on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of the title, it does say, "Minutes of the 203rd Session."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, about the middle of the page in the B/C/S version, can we see that this session started at 11.00 a.m. that day?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then if we look underneath, we can see the list of the names of the members of the Presidency that attended the session; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but with lots of crossings out, lots of names crossed out. Obviously, the list had been prepared beforehand, prior to the session itself. And why am I saying this? Because at that time, Fikret Abdic -- neither Fikret Abdic nor Dr. Nenad Kecmanovic were members of the Presidency, and you can see that prime minister was Haris Silajdzic and not Jure Pelivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. We can see from this document that Sefer Halilovic attended. Is that in his capacity as an extended member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the War Presidency, the commander of the Territorial Defence Staff is, by virtue of his office, also a member of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, on the same page in the B/C/S version, it sets out the agenda of the session. But if we can move to the next page, page 3 of the English version, to see what those points were. For some reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The next page starts at item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, for some reason I've got -- it says, "Document," but it's -- we'll have to go back to the prior page. It's point 1 I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, we can see that the first item listed on the agenda was: "Organisational and personnel changes in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Armed Forces"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe we started back at quarter to 11.00 -- sorry, quarter to 10.00. I'm just wondering if this is an appropriate moment to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How long are you going to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: We're likely to be a little while with this document, or certainly this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then if it is convenient to you, it will be convenient for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, we were dealing with the minutes of the Presidency meeting. If I could now show you page 3 in the Bosnian document and page 4 in English. If we could scroll to the top of the page in the Bosnian, please, and similarly in the English. General, can we see here that once again this page confirms that the Presidency session began at 1100 hours, 11.00 a.m. on the 8th of June? And if I could just refer you to the top right-hand corner of that document.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "1100 hours" and the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And again underneath we can see who the members of the -- who the members are at the session?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then if we scroll down the document, would you agree that what it shows on this page is the minutes, what was discussed by the various persons attending the session? If we can perhaps turn to the next page in B/C/S just to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, if we can please turn to page 6 in the English document and page 7 in the B/C/S. If we could scroll down the page back to where we were in English, please. Now, I'm not sure exactly where this appears in the B/C/S version, so please bear with me, but in the English document, in the bottom quarter, we can see that following the final comment from --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but we are unable to hear interpretation into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Interpretation into B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. So in the English version, I'm interested in the bottom quarter of this document. I'm not certain where it appears on the B/C/S version. I think it should be at the top of this page, if we can scroll up, please. Can you see there that after the final minute of what was said by a person attending the session, in this case Sefer Halilovic, you can see there that it says: "Resumption at 1400 hours." Do you see that? I'm told that actually appears on the previous page in the B/C/S, so perhaps if we can just go back, please, on the B/C/S version, on the bottom. Would you agree with me, General, that after the entry relating to Sefer, it states there: "Resumption at 1400 hours"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sefer said, "Nobody will take the rifle from my hand, and I do not accept the proposals without the opinion of the Staff. "Resumption at 2.00."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page in the Bosnian version, please. So following the resumption of the session at 2.00, can we see here an entry under "Alija"? And then if we can turn to the next page in the English version. I apologise that the two documents are not particularly synchronised. We can see, General, can't we, that after that entry for Alija, and in English I'm referring to about a quarter of the way down the page, that a vote took place? It states: "Voting results. They are all for the decision." Do you see that in the Bosnian version? It should be about the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to go further down to see what the president said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, before we go further down, General, would you agree with me that there is an entry there that says: "Voting results: They are all for the decision," and underneath it states: "Halilovic - abstention from voting"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my text. However, in my text it says that Alija Izetbegovic explained that Divjak had said that Sefer should not be changed. And then it says that Siber seconded that proposal as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can please go down in the B/C/S version. It's the middle section. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you read that -- do you see that section, General, which has just been highlighted?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That part is missing. We would have to go down, further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the Court's permission, it is a poor-quality document on the screen, could I please show the witness a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means, if there is no objection from the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says that all were in favour, apart from Halilovic, who abstains.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And does it also say "voting results" just before that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sentence before that reads: "Sefer," under 1, "read the report for the 10th Mountain Brigade, Musan Topalovic." And, second, he informed about a football game in Dobrinje. As stated here, it can correspond to a vote taking place based on a report submitted by the commander in charge before that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, again, if you could just read out the part after that, please.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 2: "Situation Gorazde."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, General, would you agree with me that from this document, we can see that the members of the Presidency have taken a vote about something?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the way it can be read from the minutes, I can only suppose or guess what the decision they voted on actually was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. If we can just go down the page a little, do you see an entry under where it says "Pejanovic," do you see where it says: "Sefer tendered his oral resignation. The president wants it in writing"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Sefer orally submitted his resignation. The president wanted to have it in writing. The rest was against."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then underneath that, do you see it states: "Hand-over between Sefer and Rasim Delic will be done during the day"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and also members of the commission are mentioned, with me included.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. Would you agree with me, General, that the decision that has taken place after the Presidency session resumed at 2.00 p.m. was the decision on whether to appoint General Delic as commander of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the Presidency's decision, to appoint General Delic commander of the Army of the Republic of B and H.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that it wouldn't be a simple task to suddenly appoint a commander of the Main Staff during wartime? That is a matter that would require some discussion and consideration; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean that it was up to General Delic to give it some thought or was it up to us in the Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, we can see that you were appointed as a member of a hand-over commission. Is that right, do you remember being appointed as a member of the hand-over commission?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember fully well that I was made a member of the commission, together with Mr. Muslimovic and Dr. Konjicija.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And it's correct, isn't it, that the purpose of a hand-over commission being appointed that day was so that the commission could sit and consider and discuss relevant issues relating to the hand-over? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And after the commission had carried out those discussions, it was then supposed to report back to the commanders' collegium?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, if we could put this document to one side for a moment, I would -- I would like to refer the witness to PT -- Prosecution document PT1195. For the purposes of the Trial Chamber, if I can explain that this document we're about to see is an extract from General Divjak's diary. Now, the relevant part that I'm interested in is in the bottom half of --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. May I object?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: According to our record, it looks like this is from another person's diary. I don't know if my learned colleague made a ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's our understanding that this is General Divjak's diary, and I'm sure he can tell us whether or not it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my diary, an excerpt from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, General, the part of the diary I'm interested in is in the bottom, at the bottom third. It's spread across the screen, so you'll have to bear with me. If we can just start at the part which has the red highlighter, the highlighted section. Is it correct that it states there: "Meeting, summoned to president"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, this is stated in the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you recall, General, is this your note of what happened -- or your -- is this your note of your involvement in the events that took place at the Presidency on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the Presidency, itself, but in contact with the president of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. So under the heading "Meeting, summoned to the president," it states there: "Delivery and examination of proposals for staff changes." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could scroll across to the right-hand side of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: For this particular entry, General, we can see there what looks to be two timings, 13.50 - 1400 hours. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, General, is it correct to say that you were summoned to the Presidency or to the president to examine proposals for staff changes at some time between 1.50 and 2.00 p.m. on the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The president asked for me to come, and handed me over four pages containing a proposal that the army commander, chief of staff, deputies and certain commanders of the Corps be retired or awarded a higher rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask for clarification. Isn't this the document that talks of, in the previous page, of a resumption of the meeting at 2.00, or am I thinking of a different document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's a different document, I believe, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, if we could scroll back across, please, to the left-hand side of the diary again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Having told us, General, that you received four pages containing a proposal, if we can look at the next entry, it states: "Meeting with Muslimovic"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we conclude with the first part? We shouldn't move on without dealing with the first part in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Certainly, General. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a summons in front of Izetbegovic's office --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The President Izetbegovic actually handed me a paper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- stating, "Have a look at this and tell me what you think," so I did. I said that Sefer Halilovic should not be dismissed from the duty of commander. And the president asked me why. I said, "I have no information as to what Mr. Delic did during the year of the war," to which Mr. Izetbegovic responded by saying that he organised 58 companies for special-purpose production. I didn't know about that. However, some other ideas went through my head at the time, but I did not share them with him. As for the other proposals, I was against them. This entire episode lasted for only six or seven minutes. Do bear that in mind, please. I was against, for example, the 6th Corps being formed, and I was against certain officers to be promoted to the rank of general. It all took place within the six or seven minutes, and I wrote down "1350 to 1400".

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then, General, just if we can cast our minds back to the last document, we know from the last -- from the minutes of the Presidency session that the Presidency session resumed at 1400 hours. Do you have recollection of the Presidency session? Well, let me rephrase that. What I'd like to go back to, General, as I indicated earlier, was the next entry in this diary. Do you see the part that says: "Meeting with Muslimovic"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could you read out to us what it says underneath, please?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I was informed by the commission in charge of the hand-over of duties." That's all it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, you were a member of that hand-over commission, you've told us. If we can scroll across to the right-hand side of the document, we can see again two timings. It says "1650" -- sorry, "1615 - 1645". Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the time when the commission was being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can go back over to the left-hand side of the page to the next entry, can you read out for us what that says, General?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Commission discussion concerning Halilovic's dismissal."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, again, if we can have a look at the --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it says "Sefer Halilovic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we get the English part of this, what has just been referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears on the page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says the commission's talk or discussions with Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not discussing his dismissal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And again, General, if we can please take a look at the right-hand side of your diary entry. So you've told us that there was commission talk or discussions with Sefer Halilovic. Under this entry, we again can see two timings, "1650 - 1715". Does this entry mean that the hand-over commission met with Sefer Halilovic between these two times?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commission meeting with Sefer Halilovic lasted for 25 minutes, from 1650 until 1715.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, General, while we're still on this side of the page, can we see that the next entry underneath, "1750", it says there -- well, let's stay on this page. The next entry, General, could you read out for us what that says?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Commanders collegium meeting."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, again, if we could please have a look at the right-hand side. Is it correct, General, that the timings of that commanders collegium meeting was from 1745 to 2030?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I noted in the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Is it correct to say, General, that it was only during the commanders collegium meeting that General Delic was appointed as commander of the Main Staff or certainly informed of ...?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanders collegium was at that moment notified that General Delic, following the Presidency's decision, was appointed army commander. General Sefer Halilovic was appointed chief of staff. Siber and I were appointed army commanders' deputies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And was General Delic present at that commanders collegium meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, it's right to say that it was during that commanders collegium meeting that General Delic was informed for the first time that he had been appointed as commander of the Main Staff, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, could that document be please made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you will allow me a comment which I think would be beneficial.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Please go ahead, General.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Delic was very embarrassed to attend that meeting, because a number of the participants in the meeting, especially members of the Patriotic League, gave comments to the effect that they would not allow that to happen. General Delic says that he was surprised when this was offered to him, that actually he in no way sought to impose himself for that position. And I think that one of the things which was said -- which he said, rather, was that, "I shall do everything to live up to the trust placed in me."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to -- this document can be put away. Thank you, Judge -- Your Honour. Can I just clarify? Has an exhibit number been assigned to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Exhibit 354.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General Divjak, I'd like to turn to General Delic's first meeting as commander of the Main Staff with his chiefs of administration. Please, can I show you Defence document D371. Your Honours, I should say this is a very short translation, just the one small extract from the diary. General Divjak, if you could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's still the witness's diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could you confirm for us, General, is this a copy of a document from your diary?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, I wonder, please, could we show General Divjak the right-hand side of this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General, can you confirm that this is an extract from your diary for the 9th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And we can see there a timing, is that correct, 10.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could please go over to the left-hand side of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Please, could you read out for us what this entry states?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Briefing the Commander." Under "1. Delic": "Greetings. Wants cooperation. Will do his utmost with help from his associates," the idea being that he would render assistance to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to effectively carry out its tasks, and he's insisting on cooperation and assistance from the Staff organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And by saying he wants assistance from the Staff organs, is it correct that at this meeting he was meeting with the chiefs of administration?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the chiefs of administrations and representatives of other organs, with the assistants as well. I was there, myself, as was Siber. We can ascertain that a bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If you can answer just "yes" or "no," can you remember what was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read what I wrote in my diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could you confirm for us, General, is it right that the chiefs of administration gave General Delic a presentation about their areas of authority?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not their powers that they spoke about, but they spoke about the goals, objectives, materiel support and personnel questions which fell within the purview of their respective administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So they were giving him information and making him aware of what was going on in the Main Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General Divjak, I'd like to refer you to your statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecution in September 2005. And at page 40 of that document, which is on the first tape of the interviews that took place, you said: "According to the way he showed his interest, he did not seem to know everything." Do you remember -- first of all, you were talking about General Delic at that point during the interview, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and I was talking about that day, the day of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And in the OTP interview, you went on to say, in connection with General Delic: "He seemed interested, not superficial. He was very carefully listening, but my conclusion was he did not know the complete situation." Is that right? Was your impression that General Delic --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and I confirm now what I said then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So it follows that your impression was that at that first meeting on the 9th of June, 1993, between General Delic and the chiefs of administration, he was for the first time really finding out what was going on within the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not what I said, and that is not what I say now. What I do say is that he -- he was objectively in no position to know some things. He just couldn't be aware of the problems of the operations, the administration, because he probably had information to the effect that the operations administration had 150 staff, whereas at the time it only had 20 people. So this is the kind of information that I'm talking about. Of course, as a member of the army, he knew what the problems of the army were. But in view of the things that he asked about, in terms of what was going on in the staff, I concluded that he was not aware of some of the things and of some of the problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we pause a little bit and allow the interpreter an opportunity to drink of water. You may proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, please could we have an exhibit number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: No. I'm tendering it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 355.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General Divjak, I'd now like to turn to the issue of the Mujahedin. And you have told the Trial Chamber about a meeting that took place on the 18th of June, 1993, where you received information mentioning the Mujahedin. And you also told us that a proposal was given to General Delic and to be discussed with President Izetbegovic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You told us how two options were proposed to General Delic to discuss with President Izetbegovic, the first being to send the foreigners back to wherever they came from, or the second being that they should be organised as a unit. Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just so that we're absolutely clear what we're talking about, I'd like to refer you to -- again to your statement given to the Office of the Prosecution in September 2005. And during that interview, the investigator put it to you very clearly whether at that meeting the discussion was about either a group or a unit. And what your response to the investigator was that they talked about a group of Mujahedin. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assert that now as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You also told us yesterday that according to the information you received, the Mujahedin were not participating in operations with members of the army. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about combat operations; right? Not just operation -- or combat activity, rather. "Operations" means also the use of also platoons and different branches.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, General, we are talking about combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excellent, thank you. According to that information, we had no data that they were engaged in combat activities with members of the army, so I'm just talking about what we knew according to the information that we had received and that we were discussing -- that we discussed on the 18th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, General. Now, in connection with that meeting, if I could please show you an exhibit. It's Exhibit 163. Your Honours, just by way of explanation, this is an order from Rasim Delic, dated 16th of June, 1993, to the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to read that document, General?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, General, that what this document shows is that General Delic is ordering the commander of the 3rd Corps to carry out certain tasks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And we can see here that it states, in the first paragraph: "Volunteers from foreign countries and a group of Bosnians trained in a so-called Gerila unit have been staying on the territory of Zenica. With the aim of their focused engagement in our struggle, I hereby order, 1, send these groups to Igman to join the SVK Independent Detachment, to Zuka's unit. Otherwise, they should have hospitality withdrawn and possibly be disarmed." Do you agree, General, that the two options mentioned in this order match or are very similar to the proposal that was put to Rasim Delic during that meeting on the 18th of June?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is obvious from this order that General Delic was aware of the existence of these groups of volunteers, of Bosnians, too, not of Bosniaks, so of Bosnians, because there is a distinction to be made between Bosnians and Bosniaks, and that they were to be trained for something -- I don't know about this Gerila group, but obviously it was the intention of the commander for that group to be comprised within the Independent Detachment of the Staff of the Supreme Command, or as we called it, "Zuka's unit," the objective being to soldierise them, which is the term I would use, which is actually to say to put them under the command of the Bosnian Army. And what is of the essence, he also ordered that if they did not obey, that they would have to be told that they were no longer welcome and be disarmed. As regards the actually undertaken measures and the results achieved, the Staff was to be informed of those as early as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that, General. So would you agree that the options, the two options contained in this order were effectively the same as that proposal which was discussed at the meeting, which you said occurred on the 18th of June?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General, the Defence has reviewed your diary entries for the 18th of June, and we can certainly provide a copy of it to you, if you'd like to see it. But it would appear that there is no mention made of a meeting taking place on the 18th of June, and my question to you is: Is it possible that that meeting, at which the Mujahedin was mentioned and the two -- and the proposal was put to General Delic, actually could have taken place prior to the 16th of June?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if my diary states the 18th, it must have been the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Sorry, General. Just to clarify, myself, the Defence team has reviewed your diary entry for the 18th, and it doesn't mention anything about meetings taking place that day. Certainly, there's no mention of any discussion -- there's no mention of any meeting at which Mujahedin are discussed. Is it possible that, in fact, the meeting at which the Mujahedin was mentioned actually took place at an earlier date before the 16th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if anyone has a better diary, let them offer it to me and to the OTP. I believe --.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not quite sure what the end of the sentence was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I give the witness a Bosnian version of his diary so he can consult it in respect of the 18th of June so that he would be better equipped to reply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know whether your opposite member wants to see it first.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's -- no, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the transcript or, rather, the conversation, the talk which I had in 1995, is reference to a document, but I don't know what document. So could I ask you kindly to tell me what is written there in the transcript of that particular interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, I'm afraid -- I'm not sure what documents you were shown during that interview. We have been provided with extracts from your diary relating to June 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't want to make a suggestion, but I don't know if he's talking about the transcript of his statement in 2005, I don't know, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, he started off by saying in the transcript, but then said, "Rather, no, the conversation or talk which I had in 1995".

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: What I would like to focus on, General, if I may, is: Do you agree that in front of you is a copy of the pages from your diary for the 18th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I noted on the 18th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you've now had the chance to review the pages from that particular date. It's right to say, isn't it, that nowhere within those pages is there any reference to a meeting at which the Mujahedin was mentioned or discussed?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, what I have here written down for the 18th, that is not the case, there is no such reference. As a matter of fact, General Delic did not at all attend this meeting on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, then, General, is it possible, then, that the meeting which you described to us in your evidence at which the Mujahedin was mentioned actually took place earlier and before the 16th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please be given today or tomorrow, or any day, my own diary so that I could consult my diary to check the entries against those dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence would have no objection to that course of action.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour. We are currently in possession of the diaries, so I'd have to have someone from the Registry get -- I'll give them to the Registry and they can give them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You can do that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right after this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: All right. We'll put that issue to one side, then, until the General's had a chance to see the documents. If I could turn to another extract from General Divjak's diary. This extract is dated the 12th of July, 1993. It is document D372. Again, Your Honours, we have just copied the relevant extract -- we've translated the relevant extracts from the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, can you tell us what it says at the top of the page, the first entry in the diary for this day?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The aggressor, on the 6th of July, a helicopter descended" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Sorry, General, I apologise. Could you just read out the heading, the top two lines of the document, for us?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first line is: "Content," and the second is: "Briefing."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could we please scroll across to the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "The 12th of July, 0900 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we could go further to the right, please, could you read out what that says?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Present, 23. Later -- arrived later, the commander, the chief of staff, and Celjo [Realtime transcript read in error "Celo"]," and that is at line 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, General, on the 12th of July at 9.20, is it correct to say that a meeting took place between yourself, the commander, the chief of staff and somebody called Celjo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt you? Could the Court Officer please shift the microphone from directly under the nose of the witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, would you like me to repeat my last question or do you still remember what I said?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting began at 9.00. At 9.20, arrived the commander, the chief of staff and Celjo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can please turn to page 2 in the English document and page 3 of the Bosnian version. Your Honour, before I proceed to ask any further questions, if I could just please ask that the record be corrected. The name of the third person attending was "Celjo" and not "Celo" as has been recorded on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What page and what line of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the same page, 84, line 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the record show that that "Celo" at line 13 should read "Celjo." Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My colleague is just pointing out that there were earlier references as well, so if they could also be amended as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If the earlier references can be also amended. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General, if you could look at the bottom of this page, entry E, it's in the bottom quarter of this page, could you read out what "E" says, please?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Security Administration." It continues to state that: "The 10th Mountain Brigade --" there is a mention of personnel changes within the Security Administration. I cannot read the rest. There is a mention further down of the formation of the Muslim Armed Forces, but I cannot read the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I apologise, General. It's because the text continues over. Perhaps the easiest thing to do, Your Honours, is if I could again please give a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, could you start from the beginning again? I apologise for not spotting that problem.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under "E," it says: "Security Administration," then: "The 10th Motorised -- the 10th Mountain and the 9th Motorised Brigade are out of control." It is suggested that personnel changes should occur in those brigades. The second item: "There is division and conflict between the civilian authorities and the 3rd Corps. There is a tendency within the 3rd Corps that the Muslim Armed Forces be formed. And this sentiment tends to spread to the 2nd Corps as well. Then in the 2nd Corps it is possible to have incidents occur."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: What it essentially describes is that at the meeting, some of the discussion focused upon the Muslim Armed Forces and problems that they were creating; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the Security Administration's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. What I'd like to do is refer -- refer further down the document, where you recorded something that General Delic had to say at this meeting. So I think just before we look at the comment of General Delic, I think we have to look at page 3 of the English version and page 5 of the Bosnian version. Your Honours, with your permission --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, General, can you see there that -- can you see there that you've written the name "Delic" and we can see a number of points underneath the name "Delic"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Commander Delic conveying certain conclusions and appointing different people to implement certain tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, the relevant point that I'd like to draw your attention to is on the next page on the B/C/S version and also the next page in the English, so page 4. Now, General, I'm interested in an entry towards the top of the second page of that document you've got there. Do you see where it says something like: "Ask for information about the situation in the 3rd Corps ..."

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Please, would you read out the entry that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ask for information on the situation in the 3rd Corps (the forming of the MOS, the Muslim Armed Forces) and send a letter to the president that they cannot act outside the framework," or the institution of the army. What I had in mind there was the MOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, General, what happened then was at this meeting General Delic made this statement, and this is what you recorded in your diary about that statement?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not an opinion. It was General Delic's order, to take certain measures and to forward information on the situation in the 3rd Corps, as well as to send a letter to the president to the effect that no activity of these units will be allowed that would fall outside the framework of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So General Delic made it clear he was going to act in this way; is that so? He was going to -- he was going to take action in connection with the Muslim Armed Forces?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was an order sent to the Operational Staff to draft such an order and to draft the letter mentioned. That was his order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, please, can I tender this document for -- into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 356.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And now, General, if I could please show you Exhibit 225, which is a document headed "Warning" from General Delic, dated the 27th of July, 1993. General Divjak, please, could you read this document?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out loud or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Not out loud. If you could just read it to yourself, please. Perhaps if we could scroll down to the bottom of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you confirm, General, that this document was sent from General Delic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, General Delic sent this to the Staffs in Sarajevo, Tuzla, Zenica, Bihac, Mostar and Gorazde, as well as to the Commands of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And we can see from this document, General, that General Delic states: "It has been registered that a number of units of the Muslim Armed Forces have been formed within the formation structure of brigades and battalions of the Army of BiH." In the second paragraph, it goes on to say: "Take all measures to prevent these and other activities aimed at breaking up that unity and to bring all armed formations under the single system of command and control." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And would you agree that the subject matter of this document is the same subject matter that General Delic discussed during the meeting that you wrote about in your diary on the 12th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the items or things discussed at the meeting, there is a mention of the MOS, but as to the fact that it was formed within brigades, there was no discussion of that at the meeting when we were issued tasks by Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, would you agree that the issue of the Muslim Armed Forces having been discussed at the meeting on the 12th of July, this document dated the 27th of July suggests or shows that General Delic reacted to the problem relating to MOS?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one of the previous documents, we can see that he had reacted previously when he said that the Zulfikar unit was supposed to be sent to Igman so that they would be included in the chain of command. Therefore, his reaction preceded this thing that you mentioned now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, General, that this document again shows that General Delic reacted quickly and took concrete measures to deal with the problem that was discussed with him?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I have the diary, Your Honour. Sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt my learned colleague, but I was just showing him that the diary has arrived, if you want to cover that today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, the diary has arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I propose, it's 1.45, I propose that we adjourn for today. I don't have a great deal of questions for tomorrow, but I think it would be sensible to deal with the diary during the adjournment overnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will then take an adjournment and come --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Robson. What did you say about the diary overnight?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I propose that General Divjak take a look at it after this court session and we deal with it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would propose that he reads the diary in court tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We'll take an adjournment for today and reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24
